clue.text: Air Force One for example key in visits

indicators.note: the key is put in the middle of the visits

parts.note: calls in = visits, pays a call on

explanation.surface: Someone boarding the presidential plane has to punch a key into a keypad on each visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key in' reads as one phrasal verb, typing something; split it and 'in' becomes a container instruction, so the key sits within the second word of the visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Force One is the call sign used by whatever aircraft carries the US president.

clue.text: Dispute on chairs around piano

indicators.note: the letters for 'on chairs' go around the piano

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over who gets the chairs arranged round the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On chairs' is a description of sitting, so it gives SAT, which then wraps P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spat is a small, short-lived quarrel.

clue.text: Proust reinterpreted produces mental dullness

indicators.note: reinterpreting Proust recasts his letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A new reading of Proust's long novel leaves the reader numb with boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that Proust's famously long novel could send anyone into a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of dulled or near-absent mental awareness.

clue.text: American doctor on course read up about certain glands

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards runs the word backwards

parts.note: a lane is a course, as on a running track

explanation.surface: A US physician on a medical course is reading up on the endocrine system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On course' looks like 'studying'; here 'on' only places A DR before the course, which is then turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenal is an adjective meaning relating to the adrenal glands, which sit above the kidneys.

clue.text: Delivery option from Carson's top department

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Carson, its top in a down clue

explanation.surface: A shopper picks a home-delivery option in the best department of Carson's store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a shopping word on the surface but a childbirth word in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A C-section, or caesarean, is one way a baby can be delivered.

clue.text: Sausage not entirely uniform sounded most unsatisfactory

indicators.note: not all of 'livery' is used, so its last letter goes
the word is only said, so the answer takes its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: most unsatisfactory = worst, said in a way that is spelt WURST

explanation.surface: A sausage served with a uniform made the worst impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Livery is the uniform worn by servants of a great house or company.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: liverwurst is one German kind of sausage, made from liver.

clue.text: First person ousted by more cheeky supporter taking cup

indicators.note: the first person is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: saucy = cheeky, so more cheeky = saucier
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: The leader is pushed out by a bolder backer who grabs the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter taking cup' sounds like a football fan with a trophy; the cup is a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the saucer holds the cup up, so it is the supporter that takes a cup.

clue.text: Rugged comedian swallowing favourite drug

indicators.note: the comedian takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a card is a joker, a funny person
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A craggy comic takes his favourite drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugged' reads as rough-featured; here it means covered with rugs.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Rugged' is read literally as 'fitted with rugs', a sense the everyday word never has.

clue.text: In recession the Parisian rents increase continually

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: Even in an economic downturn, Paris rents keep going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' looks like money paid for housing but is the noun for tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to rise steadily and uncontrollably, as prices do.

clue.text: Brahms not having to defect?

indicators.note: 'not having' means lacking, so the word goes without the TO

parts.note: Brahms (and Liszt) is rhyming slang for pissed, drunk, so blotto

explanation.surface: Must Brahms be free of the obligation to switch sides?
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed', meaning drunk, which is BLOTTO; 'to defect' reads as a verb but 'defect' is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a blot, like a defect, is a flaw that spoils something.

clue.text: Aura surrounds Conservative, one showing foreknowledge

indicators.note: the aura goes round the other letters

parts.note: presence is an aura, an impressive bearing

explanation.surface: A Tory politician has an air about him, as if he can see the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One showing foreknowledge' looks like a person with foresight; 'one' is I, and 'showing' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescience is knowledge of events before they happen.

clue.text: Famous horse corrected evil in small rook

indicators.note: correcting the word puts its letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A famous horse has been cured of its bad behaviour, as has a little chess piece.
explanation.walkthrough: S and R are standard abbreviations, and 'in' sits the rearranged EVIL between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is the Lone Ranger's horse in the Western stories.

clue.text: Disease expert treated visitor stuffed with Christmas cake?

indicators.note: the rearranged visitor has the cake inside it
the visitor's letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: a Yule log is a Christmas cake; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a visitor who has eaten too much Christmas cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' belongs to the doctor in the surface, but it works on the visitor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by field: the study of viruses is a branch of disease science, so its practitioner is a disease expert.

clue.text: Daughter leaving waterside in distress, so to speak

indicators.note: letters in a state of distress are thrown out of order
the daughter departs from the word

explanation.surface: A daughter walks away from the riverbank, upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from WATERSIDE first, then rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As it were' and 'so to speak' both soften a figurative phrase.

clue.text: Suggestion husband ignored: discourteous to butt in

indicators.note: the husband is left out of the word

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion; lose H = husband

explanation.surface: The wife hinted, the husband took no notice, and interrupting would be impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: H for husband is the standard abbreviation from genealogy and forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to enter a conversation or place uninvited.

clue.text: Country crowd at last sail from shore to island

indicators.note: only the final letter of 'crowd' is used

parts.note: a jib is a triangular sail
a boat out is away from the shore

explanation.surface: A crowd finally sets sail from the coast for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' feels like 'finally' in the story, but it takes only the D at the end of crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Sound asleep, embracing Kelvin, having left dive?

parts.note: a snore is a sound made asleep

explanation.surface: Someone fast asleep hugs Kelvin after leaving a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound asleep' reads as deeply asleep; it is the noise a sleeper makes. The question mark flags that 'dive' is loose: snorkelling is swimming near the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To snorkel is to swim face-down using a breathing tube, a shallow sort of dive.

clue.text: Those from around these parts, and alien near them?

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, turned into something unfamiliar

explanation.surface: Locals wonder whether there is an alien living close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like a noun in the surface, a creature from outer space, but it is an adjective saying 'made strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthmen are people from Earth, 'these parts' as a space visitor would say.

clue.text: Warm, feathery layer for barbarian

parts.note: a hen is a feathered egg-layer

explanation.surface: A cosy layer of down is offered to a savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feathery layer' reads like a quilt or insulation, but a layer is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathen is a scornful word for an uncivilised person, a barbarian.

clue.text: Policeman, not soft, retrained for pit

indicators.note: the policeman is trained all over again, into a new arrangement
the soft letter is not kept

parts.note: p = piano, soft in music; removed

explanation.surface: A tough police officer is retrained for work down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'Policeman' is used as letters, not as an officer to be swapped for a synonym like COP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit is the everyday British word for a coal mine, as in pit village and pitman.

clue.text: Lonely type behind upwardly mobile Chinese people

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards runs the word backwards

parts.note: to be behind something is to be pro it, in favour
the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: A lonely figure trails behind socially ambitious Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word and 'upwardly mobile' like social climbing; in fact 'behind' means supporting, PRO, which the second phrase sends upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a child without parents is pictured as alone in the world.

clue.text: One after another mentioned trainee

indicators.note: the phrase is only said, so the answer takes its sound

explanation.surface: Trainees are named one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' and 'intern' sound alike in British English, where the r is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both work for experience while learning the job.

clue.text: Popular monarch stopping street advertising

indicators.note: the monarch plugs the street, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A well-loved king blocks the road for publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: An insert is an advertising leaflet slipped inside a newspaper or magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An insert is a loose sheet of advertising put inside a publication.

clue.text: Toilets unfortunately blocked with animal body part

indicators.note: the animal sits inside the rearranged toilets like a blockage
the toilets have gone wrong, their letters out of order

explanation.surface: The loos are blocked, sadly, by some part of an animal's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal body part' runs together as one phrase, but 'animal' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the flap in the throat that covers the windpipe when you swallow.

clue.text: Penny leaving store to tour old London area

indicators.note: the penny departs from the store

explanation.surface: Penny walks out of the shop to explore a historic part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' reads as describing the London area but is its own letter, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, known for nightlife and theatres.

clue.text: Pieces for one not completely secure

indicators.note: the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: secure = firm, steady; the whole word less its final letter

explanation.surface: Items for a single person are not entirely safe.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLI is the Italian plural of solo, used in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Solos are pieces for one performer, and soli is their plural.

clue.text: Fish tails in horse meat for dog

indicators.note: the tails of the words are their last letters

parts.note: last letters of horse and meat

explanation.surface: Fish tails mixed into horse meat as dog food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish tails' pairs naturally, but 'tails' belongs with 'horse meat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound.

clue.text: Recorded fragment about tailless bird

indicators.note: the bird loses its last letter
the fragment goes round the bird

parts.note: an end is a fragment, as in odds and ends
a roller is a bird; drop its tail R

explanation.surface: A snippet of recording about a bird with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The roller is a brightly coloured bird of Europe and Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a name entered on a register has been recorded there.
